title: Unrecognized "value" attribute.
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/ca4bc3a0f6e3ef45cdbdf1d52b7ee6b0bcdb2a99/#values

> If the element is a data element
> The value is the value of the element's value attribute, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise\.

Relevant structured data validators (namely, [schema.org validator](https://validator.schema.org/) and [Google Search rich snippet testing tool](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results?id=VM1wzNGfsGmBL849Q9e_HQ)) entirely fail to recognize attribute `value` on `<data>` element, while they recognize attribute `content` on every element. This makes it impossible for authors to create documents which follow both HTML spec **and** structured data parsers, as far as Microdata is involved.
Using RDFa is only a half-solution, as the Lite version of the syntax does not support HTML semantic markup elements (namely `<time>`, `<data>` and `<meter>`. The alternative is using `<meta>` which natively supports `content` but is not suitable for readable content which only needs a machine-readable support.

Possible solutions:

- Consider allowing attribute `content` on `<data>` element as a substitute for attribute `value`.
- Push relevant tool maintainers to follow current specs, instead of following their personal flavour of them.
